previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, severe asthma, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted for an asthma exacerbation and worsening epigastric pain. He had not followed up with specialists after a recent intubation for asthma. Initial management included bronchodilators and steroids for asthma. Abdominal pain persisted despite normal CT and ultrasound; an EGD revealed candidal esophagitis and CMV-positive gastric ulcers, leading to treatment with fluconazole and valganciclovir. An MRCP showed cirrhosis and a 6.2 cm liver nodule concerning for dysplastic changes or early malignancy, necessitating outpatient hepatology follow-up for biopsy. Asthma improved with therapy, and he was discharged home on multiple new medications with plans for pulmonology, ID, and GI follow-up. He committed to sobriety and adherence to care.
problems: Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with a history of asthma 
and multiple prior intubations for asthma exacerbation on 
chronic steroids as well as history of alcoholic cirrhosis and 
pancreatitis who presents with 3 days of rapidly worsening 
dyspnea in the setting of an alcohol binge.

ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------
# Asthma exacerbation: Has a history of recently worsening 
asthma with multiple hospital admissions and recent intubation 
at ___ and other hospitals. He was last admitted for 
exacerbation at ___ in ___. He has undergone extensive 
workup to explain recently worsening asthma, including 
Aspergillus and Strongyloides serologies, both of which were 
negative. Differential for exacerbation includes viral 
etiologies and environmental allergens. He had no evidence of 
pneumonia on CXR. On admission he received magnesium, nebulizers 
and methylprednisolone in the ED. In the ICU, he was initially 
started on methylprednisolone IV and transitioned to PO 
prednisone. He was also started on continuous nebulizer 
treatments, which were spaced out when respiratory status 
improved. He required BiPAP but never needed intubation. He was 
transferred to the floor on ___, and was continued on a 
prednisone taper, monteleukast, and alternating ipratropium and 
albuterol nebulizers. He was started on oseltamivir while in the 
ICU pending viral cultures, which was stopped when respiratory 
viral panel returned negative. ___ levels to rule out 
vasculitis were also negative. IgE levels were sent to evaluate 
his candidacy for Xolair and returned normal. The cause of his 
current and recurrent exacerbations is unknown.  At time of 
discharge his respiratory status was at baseline. He was 
discharged on a long prednisone taper (60 mg for 1 days through 
___, then 5 days 40mg, 5 days 20mg, and 5 days 10mg (finishing 
taper on ___. He was started on atovaquone for PCP 
prophylaxis while on a prednisone taper, and should stop 
atovaquone after prednisone finishes. He was also instructed to 
follow up with pulmonology and sleep medicine for PFTs/DLCO and 
a sleep study to evaluate for CPAP. He will need allergy testing 
after prednisone is completed to help clarify the cause of his 
frequent exacerbations. He should also possibly have a dedicated 
neck CT as an outpatient for assessment of 
tracheobronchomalacia.

# Alcohol intoxication: Patient has a history of alcohol abuse 
and withdrawal seizures. He has reportedly been sober for the 
past 6 months. He started drinking again 3 days prior to 
admission, drinking hard alcohol continuously, in an attempt to 
numb his respiratory symptoms and avoid coming to the ED. His 
last drink was at 1600 on the night prior to admission. ETOH 
level was 307 in the ED. He was maintained on CIWA scale and 
received diazepam for mild alcohol withdrawal. However, it was 
unclear if his withdrawal symptoms were instead related to 
anxiety from asthma and tachycardia from albuterol and he was 
quickly weaned off diazepam.

# Alcoholic cirrhosis: Has a history of alcoholic cirrhosis 
complicated by thrombocytopenia. He takes nadolol, 
spironolactone, lasix at home. MRCP on prior admission was 
notable for T1 hyperintense, subtly arterially enhancing nodules 
within the right hepatic lobe, spanning an area of up to 6.2 x 
2.3 cm in the axial plane. While admitted, furosemide and 
spironolactone were continued. Nadolol was held in the setting 
of asthma exacerbation. He will need outpatient follow up with 
Dr. ___ repeat imaging of liver within the next 2 months. 
Nadolol was held at discharge and he was instructed to follow up 
with his PCP regarding when to restart.

# Immunodeficiency/CMV gastritis: Secondary to chronic steroid 
use resulting in CMV gastritis and ___ esophagitis. 
Valgancyclovir was started on ___ at an induction dose of 900mg 
Q12 though patient had not been taking this for the three days 
prior to admission. He noted that he completed a course of 
bactrim for PCP ___. He had a negative HIV test in the 
past year, so his CMV gastritis was attributed to his steroid 
use. We continued valgancyclovir at maintenance dose of 900mg 
Q24. He will require a 3-month maintenance course.

# Abdominal pain: he also had a flare of his chronic abdominal 
pain. Review of prior records revealed that he presented 
similarly with his CMV gastritis. He was continued on 
valgancyclovir as above. He was also treated with hydromorphone 
while in the hospital, but weaned off and will resume Suboxone 
at discharge. 

# Bilateral lower extremity edema: Likely secondary to 
cirrhosis, though last albumin in ___ was normal. 
Differential also includes venous stasis. BNP on admission was 
unremarkable. We continued spironolactone and furosemide. His 
TTE from ___ was reviewed and revealed mild right 
ventricular dilation and normal biventricular systolic function 
so edema related to right sided failure was ruled out.

# Sinus tachycardia: Likely secondary to continuous albuterol 
nebs, though there may have been a component of alcohol 
withdrawal as well. Epigastric pain also likely contributed. He 
was maintained on CIWA scale. Abdominal pain improved with 
narcotic regimen.

INACTIVE ISSUES
---------------
# Thrombocytopenia: Has baseline thrombocytopenia, likely due to 
cirrhosis. We continued to monitor and platelets remained stable

# Atopic dermatitis: Continued cetirizine and started on 
triamcinolone cream 

Transitional Issues:
- Will need evaluation for CPAP at home; requested appointment 
with Sleep after discharge 
- Will need allergy testing after prednisone taper completed to 
assess for an explanation of why he continues to have frequent 
asthma exacerbations. 
- Will need pulmonary follow-up after discharge for his asthma. 
We have requested an appointment and the pulmonology department 
will call him to schedule this. Needs PFTs/DLCO.
- Consider dedicated neck CT as an outpatient for assessment of 
tracheobronchomalacia.

asthma exacerbation. Restart when bronchospasm resolved

taper. Stop this when prednisone taper completed.
